Definition: from G2344; to amass or reserve (literally or figuratively):--lay up (treasure), (keep) in store, (heap) treasure (together, up).
BiblicalUsage: In the Bible, thēsaurízō means to lay up treasure. In Matthew 6:19, Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth. Wherever it appears, the word means this and not something vaguer.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that God means what He says when He uses this word, and I take Him at His word. That is why I read the passages around thēsaurízō slowly, instead of hurrying past.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
